text:
Alice: CI perf suite just alerted — p95 latency up ~18% on main after the last merge. Canary rollout auto-paused.
Ben: yikes. which PR?
Alice: looks like the merge that touched batching heuristics: PR#3421 (batch-scheduler refactor). Also saw a KV cache LRU tweak landed in PR#3433. both merged around same time.
Carla: I ran the microbench locally, flamegraph shows extra scheduling overhead in the batch scheduler path for small batches. kernel selection overhead also bigger when sequence len < 64.
Mike: interesting — kernel switch cost + more frequent batch flushes could explain tail latency. Did perf-bot compare kernel selection profiles?
perf-bot: perf summary attached — p95 increased 18%, p99 24%, throughput -6% on long-seq workloads. Hotspots: batch_scheduler::flush, kv_cache::evict, kernel_dispatch::select_kernel.
Sophia: KV LRU change in PR#3433 increases eviction frequency for large KV cache sizes — that could cause extra memory churn and stalls during cache refill.
Ben: so two hits: scheduling + KV churn. Any CI trace that pinpoints which one dominates in canary?
Alice: canary traces show spikes aligned with cache miss storms, but worst spikes correlate with batches being split more often. hard to be sure.
Carla: propose bisect: revert PR#3433 first (kv LRU tweak) and run CI perf. if regressions persist then revert PR#3421. We should do isolated A/B canaries in staging first.
Mike: agree. also want to add an extra gate: CI perf job should run the synthetic long-seq profile and fail the merge if p95 increases >10% or throughput drops >8%. current threshold is 15% which is too loose.
Sophia: we already have auto-rollback on canary if p99 > SLO by 20% for 3 samples. let's tighten canary guardrails: rollback if p95 > SLO + 10% for 2 consecutive 5-min windows OR if perf-bot reports regression on synthetic suite.
Ben: +1. also add a rollout pause after 10% of traffic with human approval required if any perf metric degrades.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for release v1.12.3 paused by perf guardrail (p95 > 10% threshold).
Alice: starting bisect now. reverting PR#3433 locally: `git revert 7a2f9d3` then running `./infra/ci/perf-run --profile long-seq --runs 10`.
Carla: I can run a focused microbench against batch scheduler patch: `go test ./runtime -bench BatchScheduler -run none -benchmem`.
Mike: if KV revert fixes 90% of the regression we can land a targeted hotfix and rework the LRU behavior behind a feature flag. if not, we'll revert the scheduler patch too.
Sophia: we should also add a CI flamegraph artifact uploader so reviewers can eyeball kernel selection differences before merging. right now artifacts timeout too often.
Ben: action items: 1) Alice revert PR#3433 and run CI perf (in progress). 2) Carla run microbench + flamegraphs. 3) Mike prepare feature-flag PR for LRU tweak. 4) Ops tighten canary SLO gates and add rollout pause at 10%.
Alice: quick update — after reverting PR#3433 locally p95 dropped back to ~6% over baseline, p99 improved, throughput roughly equal. CI run queued.
perf-bot: CI perf run finished: p95 +5%, p99 +7%, throughput -1% vs baseline. Regression considered within acceptable gate.
Carla: that points the finger at batch-scheduler refactor (PR#3421) as the remaining contributor to the small extra delta.
Mike: should we continue the canary but with stricter monitoring + immediate auto-rollback if p95 > 10%?
Sophia: yes. set canary A/B: 5% traffic variant A (new), 5% variant B (baseline), monitor 1-min, 5-min, 15-min windows; trigger auto-rollback if any window breaches. also add KV miss-rate metric to SLO dashboard.
Ben: I'll update the rollout config: add `rollout.pause_after=10%`, `rollback.p95_threshold=10%`, `rollback.window=5m,2` and wire perf-bot alerts to the paging channel.
Alice: CI hotfix PR ready to reapply without PR#3433 changes, and batch-scheduler refactor left in. will proceed with staged canary using new guardrails.
deploy-bot: Canary resumed at 5% traffic with enhanced SLO gates. Monitoring channels: #eng-runtime-perf and paging on-call.
Carla: final note — we should add a lightweight kernel-selection synthetic that hits seq<64 and seq>512 paths so future merges reveal binary regressions early.
Mike: agreed. Sophia file a ticket to add the synthetic and the flamegraph artifact upload to CI.
Sophia: ticket created: INF-4729 — add small/large seq perf profiles + flamegraph CI artifacts.
Ben: thanks everyone. good catch. :thumbsup:
Alice: closing loop — if canary holds >30m with no alerts we promote. will follow up with postmortem if needed.
